command:
set -eo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
cd /tmp
echo '== kallisto quant, the complete ERR188026 run, 16 threads (salmon s box and threads) =='
T0=$(date +%s)
kallisto quant -i kallisto.idx -o out -t 16 ERR188026_1.fastq.gz ERR188026_2.fastq.gz 2> quant.log
T1=$(date +%s)
WALL=$(( T1 - T0 ))
# Flatten before declaring outputs: a /tmp/out parent would be root-owned by dockerd.
# Never rm a staged input -- host /tmp is sticky 1777 and stage-in ran as another user,
# so the container gets EPERM, which rm -f does not suppress.
cp out/abundance.tsv abundance.tsv
cp out/run_info.json run_info.json

# no python3 and no jq in this image: parse with awk, correlate with awk+sort+join
jget() { awk -F'[:,]' -v k="$1" '$0 ~ "\""k"\"" {gsub(/[^0-9]/,"",$2); print $2; exit}' run_info.json; }
NTARG=$(jget n_targets); NPROC=$(jget n_processed); NPS=$(jget n_pseudoaligned)
ROWS=$(tail -n +2 abundance.tsv | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
TPMSUM=$(awk 'NR>1{s+=$5}END{printf "%.0f", s}' abundance.tsv)
PCT=$(awk -v a="$NPS" -v b="$NPROC" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", 100*a/b}')

# Cross-code vs salmon: SPEARMAN on rank, restricted to transcripts BOTH tools detect.
# Raw TPM is not comparable -- the two use different effective-length and multimapping
# models -- so rank order is the question both can answer. Identical metric to the earlier
# small-fixture run, so the numbers stay comparable.
awk 'FNR==NR{ if(FNR>1) st[$1]=$4; next }
     FNR>1 && $5>0 && ($1 in st) && st[$1]>0 { print $1, $5, st[$1] }' salmon_quant.sf abundance.tsv > shared.txt
NBOTH=$(wc -l < shared.txt | tr -d ' ')
sort -k2,2g shared.txt | awk '{print $1, NR}' | sort > rk.txt
sort -k3,3g shared.txt | awk '{print $1, NR}' | sort > rs.txt
SPEAR=$(join rk.txt rs.txt | awk '{k=$2;s=$3;n++;sk+=k;ss+=s;skk+=k*k;sss+=s*s;sks+=k*s}
  END{printf "%.4f", (n*sks-sk*ss)/sqrt((n*skk-sk*sk)*(n*sss-ss*ss))}')
# and the raw-value correlation, to show WHY rank is the right metric rather than asserting it
PEAR=$(awk '{x=log($2+1);y=log($3+1);n++;sx+=x;sy+=y;sxx+=x*x;syy+=y*y;sxy+=x*y}
  END{printf "%.4f", (n*sxy-sx*sy)/sqrt((n*sxx-sx*sx)*(n*syy-sy*sy))}' shared.txt)

{
  echo "wall_s               $WALL   (kallisto quant only)"
  echo "n_targets            $NTARG   want 465769  (sequences in the Ensembl 116 cDNA)"
  echo "fragments_processed  $NPROC   want 15800127  (the complete run -- same count salmon read)"
  echo "quant_rows           $ROWS   want 465769  (every transcript gets a row)"
  echo "tpm_sum              $TPMSUM   want exactly 1000000  (per-million normalisation)"
  echo "pct_pseudoaligned    $PCT"
  echo "both_detected        $NBOTH   transcripts with TPM>0 in both tools"
  echo "spearman_vs_salmon   $SPEAR   want >= 0.85  (rank order -- the comparable question)"
  echo "log_pearson_raw      $PEAR   reported, NOT asserted -- see note"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt
test "$NTARG"  -eq 465769
test "$NPROC"  -eq 15800127
test "$ROWS"   -eq 465769
test "$TPMSUM" -eq 1000000
awk -v s="$SPEAR" 'BEGIN{ if (s>=0.85) exit 0; print "spearman " s " below 0.85"; exit 1 }'
echo 'SMOKE CHECK PASSED'
